FOREWORD
0.1 "Tbis Indian Standard (Firat Revision) w.~ adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 November 1977, after the draft finalized by the Fire Fighting Sectional Committee bad been approved by the Civi 1 Engineering Division Council.

0.2 Wooden extenlion ladden for fire filhtiDI purposes have already been covered in IS : 930-1977*. During the course of workins to this standard, it baa been r,lt that timber ladders being difficult to handle because of their heavy mul, orten present difficulties to the fire fighting personnel at the time or fire fighting. Aluminium ladders being lighter are BOW being preferred to timber ladders by the fire fighting penonnel. Thi. standard wa. published in 1968. Bued on the indigenous availability of aluminium section this revision haa been prepared, the principal modification being relaxation in regard to the deflection.
0.2.1 The aluminium extension ladder consilt of one main and one extending section. The design Ihall be such .s to ensure easy .tiding of the extending section without excessive clearance in the guide and over extenlion of the ladder. The extending section ihall be guided throughout the full range of extenlion in a manner such that the sections cannot separate. retaining clips being on the main section. If 10 required. an operating gear it fixed to facilitate removal or the extenmUI section for separate use. '0.3 For the purpose of decidiDI whether a particular requirement of this .tandard is complied with. the final value, obaerved or calculated, espressing the result of a teat or aDalysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960f. The number of aignifieant placel retained in the rounded off value should be the a.me u that of the specified value in this Itandard.

I. SCOPE
1.1 This standard lays down the requirements regarding material, size, mass and performance tests of aluminium extenlion ladders for fire fighting pus:poael.

2. GENERAL
2.1 Ladder - The width of the extending section inside itl strings shall be not less than 30 em- The rounds ,hall be with non-slip serrations running the full length, These shall be fixed by expanding and flaring and .hall be spaced at 25 em centre to centre.
2.2 Salet, Device - The heals of the stiles or strings of lower section ihall be fitted with rubber feet. The pawls shall be bolted to stiles or Itriogl and their action ahall be lucb that they are let for -engagement until they have been rested on a round, and trip to clear immediately the ladder i. extended.

3. MATERIAL 3.1 The aluminium alloy section for .tile. or Itrings sball conform to Grade H~20 (in WP temper ~ of IS : 3921-1966. or IS: 733-1975t.
3.2 The aluminium alloy section used tor the rounds of the ladder shall

conform to Grade HV ( in W temper) of IS :

1285�197~t.

3.3 Aluminium alloy latch Ihall be produced from aluminium alloy conforming to IS Designation A-6 orIS : 617�197~� by chill casting. S.4 Rubber feet of aluminium ladder shall have .hear bardness of ~O to 60.

4. SIZB
4.1 Extension ladders when rully extended Ihall be in tbe three sizes, namely, 4-5 m, 7-5 m and 10-5 m ( '" Fi,. 1 )�

5. MASS
5.1 The ladders shall be as light as possible, their total mass shall not exceed as given below: 4-5 m 7-5 m 10�5 m 6. TEST
REQ.UI~EMENTS

20 kg 30 kg 48 kg

6.1 De8ectioD - The fully extended ladder shall be placed across trestles, positioned 90 cm from each end, On a 30 em wide board placed across the strings at the centre of the span, a load of 373.N ( 38 kgf) shall be .applled, allowed to remain there for a period of not less than 1 minute and then removed, A load of 736 N (75 kgf) shall then be gradually applied and the deftection due to this load shall not exceed 30 em measured from the original position. The load shall then be gradually increased to 1128 N ( 115 kgf) and the additional deflection shall not exceed 50 percent of the deftection obtained with the 736 N ( 75 "kgf). There shall be no sign of distress_

6.2 StreDgtla 01 Ro. .a 6.2.-1 With the feet of the Iadder at a distance of "2-5 m in the case of
IO-Sm, 1-75 m in the case of 7�5m, and I-25m in the case of 4�5m ladder from wall, the ladder shall be fully extended and its bead rested against the wall. A load of 320 kgf shall then be gradually applied to the middle of a metal hook baving a at lealt one round in each section by means bearing surface 5 em wide and suitably lined to prevent bruising of the round. No sign of failure shall be apparent either in the round or at its junction with the strings.

or

6.2.2 The fully extended ladder shall be placed vertically and a man weighing approximately 75 kg shall jump on each round from the round immediately above. No sign of failure shall be apparent either in the round or at its junction with the strings during this test, 6.2.3 The fully extended ladder shall be placed horizontally across trestles. One man weighing approximately 75 kg shall walle over the rounds. No sign of failure shall be apparent either in the round or at �its junction with the strings during this test. 6.3 Sway - When pitched against 1-25 m, 1-75 m and 2-5 m away froID 7'5 m and 10�~ m ladders respectively ladder or one man carrying another shall not away_

a wall with feet of the ladder the wall in the cue of 4-5 m, and two men are ascending the while descending the ladders, it

7.1 Each extension ladder sball be clearly and permaneDtly marked with the following information: .) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark, if aDy; b) The size of the ladder; and c) Ye.ir of manufacture.
